description: Runtime budgets of named scenarios (#1256, Atlas 7.1.i1256): wall-clock milliseconds and per-frame JS-WASM boundary crossings. A value past its `max` (or under its `min`) is an error; one worse than main's baseline by more than `warnRatio` is a warning. Checked by scripts/runtime_budget.py (native) and scripts/profile-browser.py --budgets (browser). The deterministic work bounds stay in contract.json.

native.description: Zone scenarios on a hosted CI runner (no GPU), from mmorpg-protocol's runtime_scenarios example in release: Greyhaven zone ticks at three populations of running players, and one publication round (every viewer projected and encoded) at 256. Ceilings leave several times the headroom over a Ryzen 7 5700X (2026-11-27: tick p95 0.33 / 0.83 / 4.1 ms, publication p95 8.0 ms) so runner noise never fails; the 256-player tick stays inside one 60 Hz tick. Hosted runners are noisier than the browser's GPU machine, hence the wider warning ratio.

browser.description: Greyhaven frame scenarios of scripts/profile-browser.py (1440x900, pixel ratio 1) on a GPU machine; hosted runners have none, so CI does not run them. fps is a floor, CPU frame and phase times are p50/p95 milliseconds, and wasmBoundaryPerFrame counts each frame's JS-WASM crossings: export calls, the module's calls into JS imports (materialized JS values) and bytes copied in and out. Ceilings are the 2026-11-27 main measurement on an RTX 3060 Ti (browser-baseline.json: idle 37.5 fps, CPU frame p50 22.8 ms, render p50 15.9 ms, 1435 calls and 36727 imports a frame) plus headroom; they tighten when the #1257 frame-rate fix lands.
